evidence: Decision C: the memory models as a managed service (setup, supervision, idle release, footprint)
host: DGX Spark GB10, aarch64, 121.9 GiB unified memory, shared with other tenants; vllm/vllm-openai@sha256:48c0a41e... (the answer model's pinned image); Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B and Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B

footprint.what: both services loaded and used once (scripts/bench_memory.py), read from the container's cgroup (memory.stat), /proc/PID/status of its processes and nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps
footprint.reading: About 60 % of each service is process overhead of a full vLLM server (two Python processes with the libraries imported), not the model. The cgroup's file pages are the mounted weights' page cache and are reclaimable.

settings_tried_to_lower_it.setting: NSF_MEMORY_KV_CACHE_BYTES=67108864 (64 MiB instead of 256 MiB), max length 2048
settings_tried_to_lower_it.result: refused by vLLM at start: 'To serve at least one request with the model's max seq len (2048), (0.22 GiB KV cache is needed, which is larger than the available KV cache memory (0.06 GiB)'. 256 MiB is the minimum for a 2,048-token input; a shorter limit would save at most 0.13 GiB per service and reject long statements, so it was not adopted. `run.sh wait` failed at once on the crash loop ('embed restarted while starting').
has no effect while --kv-cache-memory-bytes is set (the engine log says memory profiling is skipped)

footprint_decision: unchanged settings; released while idle instead (below). No setting of the pinned image lowers the footprint materially.

benchmark_recheck.reading: recall identical to accel_after_memory_semantic.json (1.0 / 0.979 / 0.917 / 0.981, 3 of 10); p50 111 ms against 107 ms

first_request_after_a_start_ms.reading: a lookup allows each model call 2 s; `wait` now counts a model as ready only after one real request, so the first lookup after a start or an idle reload is not the model's first pass
